_meta: AF/G.23 round, 2026-08-13 — São Tomé and Príncipe district-tier / OGE follow-up. New primary sources: the national OGE 2026 budget law (itemizes all six São Tomé island district câmaras by organic-classification code, distinct from the Príncipe transfer already in corpus), the Constitution's Título IX (Poder Regional e Local), and Príncipe's own 2024 regional budget decree (corroborates an OGE transfer figure, but AI-summary-fetched, flagged for raw-text re-verification). Lei n.º 16/92 (Lei de Finanças Locais e Regionais) — the law actually named as the district/regional finance mechanism inside existing node st-principe-lei10-2022 — remains genuinely unlocated after extensive search this round; not minted, logged as an open lead.

reports.title: Orçamento Geral do Estado para o ano económico de 2026 (Lei n.º 3/2026)
reports.publisher: Assembleia Nacional de São Tomé e Príncipe (Ministério das Finanças — Direcção do Orçamento)
reports.description: São Tomé and Príncipe's national state budget law for fiscal year 2026 (Lei n.º 3/2026), enacted by the Assembleia Nacional and published in Diário da República I Série, N.º 18 (23 March 2026). Table 6 ("Despesas Totais por Classificação Orgânica", sourced to the Ministério das Finanças' Direcção do Orçamento) itemizes multi-year expenditure by organic-classification code for all six São Tomé island district câmaras alongside the Príncipe regional government, e.g. the row "70.0.00-GRP 109 954,0 109 651,0 128 425,0 144 075,0 107 169..." through "76.0.00-CDMZ 10 950,0 14 623,7 27 966,0 32 168,0 19 966..." (columns: Execução 2022 / Execução 2023 / OGE 2024 / OGE 2025 / Pré-Orçamento 2026, figures in thousands of dobras). Code-to-name mapping (GRP = Governo Regional do Príncipe; CDAG = Câmara Distrital de Água Grande; CDCG = Câmara Distrital de Cantagalo; CDC = Câmara Distrital de Caué; CDLMB = Câmara Distrital de Lembá; CDLOBT = Câmara Distrital de Lobata; CDMZ = Câmara Distrital de Mé-Zóchi) is inferred from standard STP abbreviation convention rather than an explicit legend in the extracted text, but is corroborated by the same table's accompanying Table 8 prose, which independently names districts by percentage: "observa-se que 89% das despesas totais são de âmbito nacional, o que evidencia a abrangência das acções governamentais. Em seguida, destacam-se Água Grande com 3%, Região Autónoma do Príncipe com 3%, Mé-Zóchi com 1% e Lobata 1%, reflectindo a distribuição das despesas pelas diferentes regiões." Article 4 §2 establishes a recurring quarterly transfer mechanism grouping Príncipe and the district câmaras together under one legal regime: "As transferências previstas no OGE para a Região Autónoma do Príncipe (RAP) e Autarquias Locais (AL) são feitas por trimestre, proporcionalmente, de acordo com o valor aprovado, conforme a disponibilidade financeira, observando o tipificado no número 1." HOSTING CAVEAT: retrieved from cipstp.st (Centro de Integridade Pública de STP, a public-integrity NGO), not a .gov.st domain; the PDF's own title page and gazette metadata (Lei n.º 3/2026, Diário da República I Série N.º 18) identify it as a direct reproduction of the official gazette text, but the official host dre.gov.st returned a TLS certificate-hostname-mismatch error and could not be independently checked this round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual state budget law (Orçamento Geral do Estado), enacted yearly by the Assembleia Nacional; this edition covers fiscal year 2026 and also reports historical execution figures for 2022-2023 and approved budgets for 2024-2025.

reports.title: Constituição da República Democrática de São Tomé e Príncipe (Lei n.º 1/2003) — Título IX, Poder Regional e Local
reports.publisher: Assembleia Nacional de São Tomé e Príncipe
reports.description: São Tomé and Príncipe's Constitution (Lei n.º 1/2003), Título IX ("Órgãos do Poder Regional e Local"), supplies the constitutional basis for both Príncipe's regional autonomy and the six-district câmara system referenced throughout the OGE 2026 budget law. Artigo 136.º ("Funções"), §3, states: "Os órgãos do poder regional e local dispõem de finanças e património próprios, de acordo com a lei." [Regional and local power bodies have their own finances and assets, in accordance with the law] — the constitutional "own finances" clause covering both tiers, leaving the specific transfer mechanism to ordinary law (supplied, per existing corpus node st-principe-lei10-2022, by Lei n.º 16/92, and for the annual budget cycle by st-oge-2026's Article 4). Artigo 139.º ("Órgãos distritais") defines the district government structure: "A organização das autarquias locais em cada Distrito compreende uma Assembleia Distrital eleita e com poderes deliberativos e um órgão executivo colegial, denominado Câmara Distrital." Artigo 142.º ("Câmara Distrital") further specifies: "1. A Câmara Distrital, constituída por um presidente e vereadores, é um órgão executivo colegial do distrito, eleita de entre os membros de cada Assembleia Distrital. 2. A Câmara Distrital é responsável politicamente perante a Assembleia Distrital e pode ser destituída a todo o tempo, nos termos da lei." The Constitution itself does not enumerate the six district names; that enumeration appears only in ordinary legislation (the OGE 2026 budget table, st-oge-2026).

reports.title: Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 02/2024 (Orçamento Regional da Região Autónoma do Príncipe para 2024)
reports.publisher: Assembleia Legislativa Regional da Região Autónoma do Príncipe / Governo Regional do Príncipe
reports.region: São Tomé and Príncipe — Região Autónoma do Príncipe
reports.description: The Príncipe Autonomous Region's own regional budget decree for fiscal year 2024, approved by the Assembleia Legislativa Regional on 28 February 2024 and published 16 April 2024, hosted on principe.gov.st (the regional government's own official site). Its preamble explicitly ties the regional budget to the national state budget's approval: "Na sequência da aprovação pela Assembleia Nacional do Orçamento Geral do Estado para o ano económico 2024 e a alteração das receitas e despesas afectas à Região Autónoma do Príncipe." Article 2 §1(b) specifies the resulting transfer line item as STD 128.425.000,00 under "Transferências de Tesouro Nacional." This figure matches, digit-for-digit, the national OGE 2026 law's own Table 6 retrospective "OGE 2024" column for the "70.0.00-GRP" line (128 425,0 thousand dobras = 128.425.000,00 dobras; see st-oge-2026), independently corroborating both documents' figures for Príncipe's 2024 treasury transfer. CAVEAT: this document's quotes were retrieved via an AI-summarization fetch pass rather than independently re-extracted from raw PDF text this round; treat as plausible pending raw-text re-verification in a future round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual regional budget decree (Orçamento Regional), enacted yearly by the Príncipe Regional Legislative Assembly; this edition covers fiscal year 2024.

dependencies.basis: The RAP's own 2024 regional budget decree states its 'Transferências de Tesouro Nacional' line item is STD 128.425.000,00, and explicitly frames this as following the national Assembleia Nacional's approval of the OGE for 2024 ('Na sequência da aprovação pela Assembleia Nacional do Orçamento Geral do Estado para o ano económico 2024...'). This exact figure (128.425.000,00 dobras) reappears digit-for-digit in the OGE 2026 law's own Table 6 'OGE 2024' retrospective column for the '70.0.00-GRP' line. Because the primary OGE-2024-specific law document is not itself in the corpus, st-oge-2026 (which independently reports and corroborates the same 2024 figure) is used as the representative national-OGE target node. CAVEAT: directionality is chronologically imperfect (the 2024 decree predates the 2026 law) — the true underlying dependency is on the actual OGE-2024 law, not literally the 2026 edition; and the RAP-decree quote itself was AI-summary-fetched, not independently raw-text re-verified this round. See corresponding _dropped caveat entry.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Na sequência da aprovação pela Assembleia Nacional do Orçamento Geral do Estado para o ano económico 2024...

dependencies.basis: INE-STP's own 'Cooperação Internacional' page names AFRISTAT and CPLP directly among multilateral/regional partners that have contributed technical capacity specifically to statistical domains including the CPI: '...Regionais: o Banco Africano de Desenvolvimento (BAD), AFRISTAT, CPLP, que têm tido um papel primordial para o instituto... na capacitação técnica em vários domínios, tais como a legislação, planeamento, classificações, conceitos e nomenclaturas, infraestruturas estatísticas, produção estatística, onde se destaca o índice de preços no consumidor (IPC)...' This is a second, independent primary source (INE's own cooperation page, distinct from the existing st-snds-2018-2021 -> afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 edge) corroborating an AFRISTAT-CPI capacity-building link, and also names a new partner, CPLP, not previously tied to CPI work in the corpus (no dedicated CPLP report node exists to target as a separate edge).

_dropped.edge: st-principe-lei10-2022 cites Lei n.º 16/92 (Lei de Finanças Locais e Regionais) — primary text
_dropped.why: Lei 10/2022 Article 101 quotes Lei n.º 16/92 by name as the governing local/regional finance law, but its own primary text remains unlocated despite extensive search this round: dgrn.gov.st directory listing (403 Forbidden), its JS-rendered legislation SPA leginon.dgrn.gov.st (no extractable static text; guessed API endpoints /api/search, /api/leis, /swagger returned 404), faolex.fao.org constructed search URLs (404), principe.gov.st and cipstp.st site searches for '16/92' (no relevant results), legispalop.org (502 Bad Gateway via proxy), and a Wayback Machine CDX API query (connection reset). Note also that dgrn.gov.st's own homepage was reached (200 OK) but contained suspicious injected spam links (diyarbakirescort.com, fastsexvideos.com, hdporn7.com), suggesting the domain may be compromised — treat any future content retrieved from it with caution. Remains a strong, worthwhile open lead for a follow-up round with headless-browser/JS-execution tooling against leginon.dgrn.gov.st.

_dropped.edge: Água Grande district government self-published website
_dropped.why: Extensive search found only third-party news coverage (Téla Nón, STP-Press, Hoje Macau, radiof.gmpress.pt) referencing 'Câmara Distrital de Água Grande,' but no official .gov.st or câmara-hosted primary site for Água Grande or any other individual São Tomé island district.

Full-text search of the entire 70-page ENDE 2025-2029 PDF (self-extracted via pdftotext) for 'distrit,' each of the six district names, and 'câmara' returned zero matches — confirmed absence of district-level content in this national statistics-strategy document, not a search failure.

_dropped.edge: INE-STP IPC 'Nota Explicativa' methodology files (COICOP/AFRISTAT/CPLP/IMF-Manual citation check)
_dropped.why: The Nota Explicativa .xls methodology files (e.g. 'Nota_Explicativa_Dezembro_2018.xls') are gated behind a Phoca Download license/terms click-through form on ine.st; the direct file URL returns only the HTML landing page, not the file itself, so no methodology-citation text could be extracted this round without simulating the JS-driven download gate.

_dropped.edge: Tribunal de Contas STP publications naming districts
_dropped.why: WebSearch budget was exhausted this session before a targeted search for Tribunal de Contas (STP's court of auditors) reports on district finance could be run. Given the strength of the OGE 2026 findings (all six districts itemized by name/code with multi-year figures), this was judged lower priority to leave open rather than a dead end — a legitimate lead for a follow-up round.

This edge is included in the dependencies array above based on a digit-for-digit match of the 128.425.000,00 dobras GRP transfer figure across both documents, but two caveats apply: (1) the RAP decree's quotes were retrieved via WebFetch AI-summarization, not independently re-extracted from raw PDF text; and (2) the target/direction is representative rather than literal — the RAP decree (2024) chronologically predates st-oge-2026 (2026) and could not literally have drawn data from it; the true source is the actual OGE-2024 law, which is not itself a corpus node. Recommend raw-PDF re-verification and, if a dedicated OGE-2024 node is later minted, re-pointing this edge to it.
